detail: Scenes 6 and 7 are the same surface with only a scroll between them, which is the rubric's explicit max-2 case. Scene 6's final frame is the 'RUTF Northeast Nigeria Q3 2026' modal opened over Ada's Solicitations list, showing the lot header, the 60,000-carton Maiduguri table (Savanna 42.29 / Kano 43.77 / Lagos 45.79 / Faso 48.64) and the first row of the Djibo lot (Faso NutriWorks SA, USD 41.85, 21d, technical 88) already visible at the bottom edge. Scene 7's final frame is the identical modal scrolled down so the remaining three Djibo rows show. Scene 7 therefore adds four table rows to a reveal scene 6 has already half-made; its removal would barely be noticed. Worse, scene 6 shows nothing of its OWN claim: 'eligibility is enforced when the payload is built, so an unqualified supplier never receives the solicitation'. Server-side eligibility gating -- one of the demo's most differentiating claims -- is not depicted in any of the nine frames. Note this defect was introduced by the fix to the previous iteration's persona finding: moving scene 6 from the supplier's screen to Ada's compare-bids modal fixed the persona mismatch and created a duplicate of scene 7.
fix_recommendation: Put scene 6 back on the supplier side, but motivate the handoff in the narration instead of leaving it unexplained. End scene 6 on Amina's 'Solicitations & bids' tab with 'RUTF Northeast Nigeria Q3 2026' present because Savanna holds a live RUTF qualification -- ideally alongside a second supplier's view (e.g. Sahel Milk Products, therapeutic milk only) where the same solicitation is simply absent from the list rather than shown greyed out. That restores a distinct surface, demonstrates the claim on camera for the first time, and leaves scene 7 as the sole owner of the per-lot comparison.

detail: The finale is now genuinely strong -- contract OES-C-2026-NG1 opened to funder US Government, appropriation 'FY2026 Famine Prevention Reserve - FY2026', IATI activity US-GOV-1-OES-OES-C-2026-NG1, USD 1,894,500 obligated / USD 842,000 disbursed 'against confirmed delivery only', and a 16-row delivery schedule -- but the record on screen is not the award the viewer just watched. Scene 8 awards the Maiduguri lot to Savanna Nutrients at 60,000 cartons, USD 42.29 per carton, USD 2,537,400. Scene 9's contract reads 45,000 cartons RUTF to Maiduguri at USD 42.10. The narration over it says 'The award is immutable -- it is the decision. What carries it out is a contract.' A procurement buyer reading the numbers sees the causal claim the whole nine scenes build toward asserted over a record that demonstrably came from somewhere else, with nothing on screen naming the source award or round. The recipe knows this (its show text says 'created from the earlier Q2 award into Maiduguri, not the one just made'); the viewer is never told.
fix_recommendation: Pick one: (a) create the contract from the scene-8 Q3 Maiduguri award live on camera, so the quantity and unit price carry through visibly; (b) surface provenance on the contract card -- a 'from award: RUTF Northeast Nigeria Q2 2026, lot Maiduguri' line -- and change the narration to name it explicitly ('an award from last quarter, already in execution'); or (c) re-order so the closing scene follows the Q2 award it descends from. Option (b) is the cheapest and removes the contradiction without touching the data.

detail: Scene 4 carries the demo's per-category-decision-with-expiry claim, and the actions do execute it (Qualify on RUTF, Reject on Therapeutic milk, Record decision -- all reported ok). But the captured frame shows none of it: Tomas's review queue with three rows, a 'Decision recorded.' toast bottom-right, and roughly the bottom half of the viewport blank white. Neither of the two opposite decisions is visible, and no expiry date appears anywhere in the frame -- the nearest evidence is scene 5's 'EARLIEST EXPIRY' column, a scene later and on a different persona's screen. This is a much weaker form of the previous iteration's 'scene 4 is scene 2 with a card deleted': the persona chip, the toast and the missing Savanna row now distinguish it, but it is still the same surface as scene 2 showing strictly less -- one row fewer, the entire 'Rounds' card and 'New round' button gone.
fix_recommendation: End the scene on the decision modal after both buttons are pressed and before 'Record decision' dismisses it, so the RUTF pass and the therapeutic-milk decline sit in one frame with the expiry the pass stamps. Failing that, capture the resulting qualification instead of the empty queue -- Savanna's registry row with 'RUTF / Jan 19, 2028' is the visible proof the scene is claiming.

detail: The opening narration states the problem well -- supplier knowledge lives in email threads and attached PDFs, so the simplest question cannot be answered without opening a folder and reading. The opening FRAME shows the answer: '14 Qualified suppliers / no near-term expiries', a coverage-by-category bar chart with every category populated, four applications queued, one live solicitation. Nothing on screen carries the pain the voice is describing; the viewer is told about a folder of PDFs while looking at a healthy dashboard. The close then answers a larger question than the opening posed (the opening's literal question is answered mid-run, in scene 5's registry), so the two ends do not clasp.
fix_recommendation: Either open on a frame that carries the problem -- an empty or near-empty registry, or the EOI round about to be published -- and let scene 5's registry be the moment the opening question is answered on screen; or re-cut the opening narration so it promises what the frame actually shows and what the close actually delivers (a supply base you can query, and a dollar traceable to a carton), rather than a folder of PDFs the demo never depicts.

detail: Six of nine frames are a data table on a white card, and scenes 6, 7 and 8 are three consecutive frames of the same white modal over the same dimmed Solicitations list. Only scene 8 earns its repetition -- the 'Awarded -- Savanna Nutrients Ltd' and 'Awarded -- Faso NutriWorks SA' pills plus the confirming toast are a real state change and should stay. This is CONCEPT, not PRODUCT: the product does have other surfaces the run is not visiting (the supplier-side console in scene 3, the filterable registry in scene 5 and the command centre's exception list in scene 9 are all visually distinct), and the narrative simply chose to sit on one modal for three beats. Credit where due -- the environment's missing Mapbox token is no longer a visual defect: the network map never appears in any final frame, because scene 9's contract modal covers it.
fix_recommendation: Fixing arc-01 (move scene 6 to the supplier side) removes one of the three modal frames on its own. For the remaining pair, consider giving scene 7 a different framing of the comparison -- the two lot cards side by side, or the modal scrolled so both leaders are in one frame -- so scene 8's return to the same layout reads as a state change rather than a fourth look at the same screen.
